answer: Honest side: an agent buys a 120-unit bond that pays no interest and loses 4% of value each epoch, but real work restores it to face value, so a working identity stays whole. Fake side: the same bond sits in a grove of idle clones, bleeding value with no work to refresh it; below 60 it is downgraded and loses rewards. A zephyr of fresh capital cannot save it; each new bond decays the same way. Fraud costs half the residual value and a 6-epoch refresh freeze. At its nadir, 1,000 clones have sunk 120,000 units, lose 4,800 per epoch, and lose 40,000 after 10 idle epochs.
